placements.why: This envelope's entire content is a deployment gate policy (signed manifests, staging/production scope, ownership) — a technical release-control decision with no existing strata category to hold it. Architecture is the org's known top-level category for this domain and nothing has been minted yet in this repo, so it is minted standalone with no required parent.
placements.title: Technical release and deployment control as an organizational category
placements.frame: What technical infrastructure and deployment-control decisions define how releases are built, gated, and shipped?

placements.title: Past incidents converted into standing deployment mandates
placements.frame: Does invoking a specific past failure function to legitimate a new standing precondition, rather than merely to explain it?
placements.why: src-1 performs the gate as a settled 'now requires' rule and src-2 grounds it in a concrete prior incident ('two unsigned artifacts reach staging... that is the whole reason for the gate'). Together they name a recurring organizational pattern — citing a past breach to justify a standing control — that future envelopes documenting other gates or controls would plausibly keep feeding, not a one-time fact.

placements.title: Deployment gates decomposed into rule, scope, and owner fields
placements.frame: When a gate is restated as fixed fields (rule / scope / owner), what does the choice of fields reveal about what the organization treats as governable?
placements.why: src-3, src-4, and src-5 share a bolded-label cadence and each fixes one operational parameter of the same gate — the rule itself, its environmental scope, and its named accountable owner. This is the recurring documentation pattern of decomposing a control into standing fields, a subject future gate write-ups would continue to feed, not a single fact about this gate alone.
